title: Working hours per day for labourers (period source)
source: Voth HJ, Time and work in eighteenth-century London, J Econ Hist 1998;58:29-58. The JEH PDF is scanned images with no text, so the figure is as Stephenson 2018 (Judy Stephenson, MPRA 84828) reports Voth's result; the Nuffield working-paper page gave an abstract only.
rows: London, from witnesses' court depositions, 1750s to 1800; Stephenson reports 'only 208 working days of 11 hours a day on average' in the 1750s
Voth's sample is wage-earning men in many trades, not only labourers; the day length did not change much in his result.
Stephenson: rose to 306 days of 11 hours.
